text_plugin_synopsis: Pinyin4j plugin for Chinese to Hanyu Pinyin conversion
p_languages_all_supported_for_readme: The README.md is currently available in the following languages
p_introduction_what: The Pinyin4j Plugin brings lightweight Chinese-to-Hanyu-Pinyin conversion to AutoJs6. Once installed, scripts can use the global object `pinyin4j` to convert Chinese text to pinyin character by character, with configurable letter case, tone format, `ü` representation and syllable separator; a utility method for turning tone-number text into tone marks is also included.
p_introduction_how: The plugin is a separately installed APK running in its own process; AutoJs6 discovers it automatically through the plugin mechanism and communicates with it via AIDL. Conversion is powered by the classic Java library [pinyin4j]({{ pinyin4j_official_url }}) (`{{ pinyin4j_library_coordinates }}`). The measured release is only 349 KiB, and all conversion happens locally on the device with no network access. Since AutoJs6 v6.8.0, the host's `pinyin4j` module is implemented by this plugin.
p_introduction_extra: This plugin and [Pinyin]({{ pinyin_repo_url }}) are sister plugins: this one offers simple and reliable per-character transcription at a tiny size, while the Pinyin plugin ships full dictionaries and Jieba segmentation, supporting heteronym disambiguation and a surname mode for accuracy-focused scenarios. Both can be installed side by side; see `Sister Plugin Comparison` below.
features: Works out of the box: automatically discovered by AutoJs6 after installation, no host restart needed; scripts use the global object `pinyin4j` directly.
Extremely lightweight: the measured release is only 349 KiB, pure JVM with no native libraries, compatible with all CPU architectures.
Three tone formats: no tone, tone numbers (`han4`) and tone marks (`hàn`), selectable as needed.
Flexible output: configurable letter case, three `ü` representations (`lv` / `lu:` / `lü`) and an arbitrary syllable separator.
Tone utility: `pinyin4j.as(text)` converts tone-number text into the tone-mark form in one step.
Lenient values: options are case-insensitive and accept several short aliases (such as `tone: "MARK"`); invalid values raise localized error messages.
Fully offline: conversion relies on bundled data and runs locally on the device, without any network requests.
Multilingual: plugin info, instructions, README and changelog are available in 10 languages.
usage_steps: Upgrade AutoJs6 to internal build {{ required_host_version_code }} ({{ required_host_version_name }}) or later; since v6.8.0 pinyin capabilities are fully delegated to plugins, so the latest version is recommended.
Download the plugin APK from the [Releases]({{ repo_url }}/releases) page and install it on the device running AutoJs6, or install it online directly from the AutoJs6 Plugin Center.
Open the AutoJs6 Plugin Center, confirm that the `Pinyin4j` plugin is recognized, then grant authorization and make sure it is enabled.
Call the `pinyin4j` global object directly in scripts, following the `Quick Start` examples below; you may also run the `Quick Self-Check` first to confirm the plugin is active.
p_usage_note: The plugin ships as a single universal package (pure JVM, no CPU architecture variants) and supports devices running Android {{ min_android_version }} (API {{ android_min_sdk }}) or later. It has no standalone UI and creates no launcher icon; AutoJs6 discovers and manages it centrally.
p_quick_start_basic: Basic conversion: lowercase pinyin without tones by default; the second argument may simply be a separator
p_quick_start_as: Tone utility: convert tone-number text into tone marks
p_options_intro: `pinyin4j.of(text, options)` supports the following options (short alias keys in parentheses)
td_option_tone: Tone format: `WITHOUT_TONE` for none, `WITH_TONE_NUMBER` for tone numbers, `WITH_TONE_MARK` for tone marks
td_option_v: How `ü` is written: `WITH_V` (`lv`), `WITH_U_AND_COLON` (`lu:`), `WITH_U_UNICODE` (`lü`); defaults to `WITH_U_UNICODE` when the tone-mark format is used
td_option_separator: Separator between syllables, any string; a trailing separator at the end of the output is removed
p_options_note: Values are case-insensitive and accept short aliases, such as `tone: "MARK"` / `"NUMBER"` / `"NO"`, `case: "UP"` / `"LOW"`, `v: "V"` / `"U:"` / `"U"`. Passing an invalid value throws an exception with a localized message.
p_script_api_intro: The `pinyin4j` global object provides the following methods (calling `pinyin4j(text, options)` directly is equivalent to `pinyin4j.of`)
api_points: `of` iterates Unicode code points and queries the pinned pinyin4j 2.5.1 dictionary directly: all 20,378 mapped BMP characters (including `〇`) convert, while unmapped and supplementary-plane code points remain intact. It still chooses only the first pronunciation, with no contextual disambiguation.
The second argument of `of` can be either an options object or a plain string used as the separator.

`as` converts only complete recognized syllables with tone digits `0`-`4`, preserves input case, and accepts `v`, `u:`, or `ü`; invalid syllables, tone digit `5`, and fragments adjacent to letters or digits remain unchanged. This method corresponds to `asTone` in the plugin's AIDL interface.
Option values are case-insensitive and accept several short aliases (see `Options` above); invalid values throw an exception with a localized message.
All methods return synchronously; the first conversion lazily loads the pinyin4j dictionary and is therefore slower than steady-state calls, as documented in the conversion benchmark.
p_self_check_intro: After installing and enabling the plugin, run this one-liner
p_self_check_result: If it prints `pinyin`, the plugin is working properly.

faq.q: How do I confirm the plugin is active?
faq.a: Open the AutoJs6 Plugin Center; if the `Pinyin4j` plugin is listed and enabled, the host has recognized it. Then run the `Quick Self-Check` script above; printing `pinyin` means it works.

faq.q: Scripts report a missing plugin or say `pinyin4j` is unavailable?
faq.a: Make sure the AutoJs6 internal build is at least {{ required_host_version_code }}, and that the plugin is installed, authorized and enabled in the Plugin Center. Since AutoJs6 v6.8.0 the host no longer bundles the pinyin4j library; this plugin provides the capability entirely.

faq.q: Why is there no plugin icon in the app list or on the home screen?
faq.a: This is expected. The plugin has no standalone UI and creates no launcher icon; after installation AutoJs6 discovers and invokes it in the background, and all interaction happens inside AutoJs6.

faq.q: Heteronym pronunciations look wrong (e.g. "重庆" is not read as chongqing)?
faq.a: This plugin converts character by character and always takes the first dictionary pronunciation, without phrase-context disambiguation; this is an inherent trade-off of the lightweight approach. For heteronym disambiguation, phrase dictionaries or surname readings, use the sister plugin [Pinyin]({{ pinyin_repo_url }}).

faq.q: Why does `pinyin4j.asTone(text)` from older docs or scripts not work?
faq.a: On the host side the method is named `pinyin4j.as(text)`; `asTone` is the method name in the plugin's AIDL interface, and both behave identically. Use `pinyin4j.as(text)` in scripts.

faq.q: Does the plugin access the network or request sensitive permissions?
faq.a: No. Conversion data is bundled in the package and conversion happens locally on the device. The manifest only declares the plugin permission needed to communicate with AutoJs6, without requesting network, storage or any other sensitive system permission.

faq.q: How do I choose between this plugin and the sister plugin Pinyin?
faq.a: Choose this plugin when you only need lightweight per-character transcription and care about package size; choose [Pinyin]({{ pinyin_repo_url }}) when you need heteronyms, segmentation, phrases or surname readings. They do not conflict and can be installed together; see `Sister Plugin Comparison` below.

p_security_intro: The plugin is designed to keep its data and permission surface as small as possible:
security_points: Minimal permissions: the manifest only declares the AutoJs6 plugin permission (`org.autojs.permission.PLUGIN`), without requesting network, storage, camera or any other sensitive system permission.
Local conversion: text to convert only travels within the device via Binder; conversion data is fully bundled, everything is offline and no data leaves the device.

Signature and authorization: AutoJs6 verifies the plugin signature, and the plugin must be authorized and enabled in the Plugin Center before scripts can call it; the service and wake entry are both protected by the plugin permission, so third-party apps cannot invoke them directly.
Open and auditable: the plugin code and its documentation pipeline are fully open source, and conversion is powered by the widely used open-source library pinyin4j.
p_security_permission: Only obtain plugin packages from the official [Releases]({{ repo_url }}/releases) page or the AutoJs6 Plugin Center; a package from an unknown source may be tampered with even if its name and version look identical.
p_sibling_intro: AutoJs6 offers two official pinyin plugins with different focuses; they can be installed side by side
td_sibling_output_pinyin: 2D candidate array (combinable via `compact()`) or compact string
td_sibling_size_pinyin: 5.95 MiB ([measured full release]({{ pinyin_repo_url }}/blob/master/docs/size/packaging-strategy-2026-09-01.md), bundled dictionaries)
td_sibling_performance_pinyin4j: Lightweight character path; [measured JVM/Android baseline]({{ repo_url }}/blob/master/docs/performance/conversion-baseline-2026-09-01.md)
td_sibling_performance_pinyin: [Measured segmenter run]({{ pinyin_repo_url }}/blob/master/docs/benchmarks/segmenter-reuse-2026-09-01.md); heavier dictionary, segmentation, and heteronym path, varying by mode
td_sibling_scenario_pinyin4j: Size and simplicity first: quick per-character transcription
td_sibling_scenario_pinyin: Accuracy first: heteronyms, phrases, person names
p_sibling_note: The two plugins are independent and never conflict; with both installed, scripts may call `pinyin4j` and `pinyin` separately as needed. See [AutoJs6-Plugin-Pinyin]({{ pinyin_repo_url }}) for details on the Pinyin plugin.
p_plugin_interface: The following information targets AutoJs6 host and plugin developers; the host uses these identifiers to discover the plugin and negotiate capabilities
p_contract_service: `Pinyin4jPluginService` responds to the `{{ discovery_action }}` action (category `{{ discovery_category }}`) and exposes 3 methods through the AIDL interface `{{ binder_interface }}`; options for `of` are passed via a `Bundle` (keys: `caseType` / `toneType` / `vCharType` / `separator`), and invalid values throw an `IllegalArgumentException` with a localized message. Both the service and `WakeActivity` are protected by the `org.autojs.permission.PLUGIN` permission, so third-party apps cannot invoke them directly.
p_roadmap: ROADMAP.md tracks evidence by milestone. M3 now has plugin-side Unicode coverage, tone-boundary behavior, and the multi-pronunciation/six-system core plus a proposed contract, while the public API still awaits coordinated host AIDL work. M4 dependency-risk, performance, size, and selection baselines are complete. Unchecked items are not current capabilities.

p_build_intro: This section targets developers who want to build the plugin from source.
p_build_release: Build a release APK (single universal package; signed automatically once signing is configured in the untracked `sign.properties`)
p_build_artifacts: For a verified release archive, run `py .python/prepare_release.py`. It checks generated docs, builds and verifies the signed universal APK, validates version metadata, calculates CRC32 and SHA-256, and atomically writes the APK, `SHA256SUMS.txt` and English `RELEASE_NOTES.md` under `app/releases/v<version>`.
p_build_params: Build parameters are centralized in `version.properties`: minimum SDK {{ android_min_sdk }} (Android {{ min_android_version }}), target SDK {{ android_target_sdk }}, current version {{ version_name }}.
p_resource_layout: `strings.xml` provides localized plugin descriptions and error messages, and `plugin_instruction.md` provides the usage instructions shown in the host Plugin Center. The README, changelog and instructions are all generated from JSON sources: after editing sources under `.readme/` and `.changelog/`, run `py .python/generate_markdown.py` to regenerate all artifacts; generated artifacts are never edited by hand. Run `py .python/generate_markdown.py --check` to verify that sources and artifacts are in sync.
